item.title: more debugging information (missing points with go-lot)
item.description:
With ggplot, I sometimes get the message:
4: Removed 291 rows containing missing values or values outside the scale range (geom_point()`).`
but this often happens on a page with multiple plots, so it is unclear where the error is.
Is there an option to make 'R' tell me what line produced the error message? Better still, to tell me which rows had the bad points?

item.title: Is R really dying slowly?
item.description: I apologize with my controversial post here in advance. I am just curious if R really won't make it into the future, and significantly worrying about learning R. My programming toolkit mainly includes R, Python, C++, and secondarily SQL and a little JavaScript. I am improving my skills for my 3 main programming languages for the past years, such as data manipulation and visualization in R, performing XGBoost for both R and Python, and writing my own fast exponential smoothing in C++. Yet, I worried if my learnings in R is going to be wasted.
